Subject: End-of-commitment opt-out procedures & termination ops pocket guide

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the time last week. Procurement asked a few clarifying questions after the demo about how we handle end-of-term and soft exits; I promised to pull together what the team typically needs to close the Order Form and minimize friction on both sides.

Attached are: 1) a focused MSA redline that isolates the auto-renew/notice language and 2) the Order Form SOW with a short note on ramp-down support. Key asks for you (and procurement):

- Confirm whether a 30/60/90-day notice window is preferred for your legal/procurement team.
- Confirm if you need a "termination for convenience" (TFC) with a pro-rated credit or a support handover fee.
- Share the procurement contact who should receive the DocuSign route (we usually route to procurement + legal).

I tried to keep the redline minimal — items highlighted: auto-renew duration, notice timing, early termination charge (if any), and handback support obligations. If you prefer a short call to walk through the options, I can loop in Karthik (contracts) and Marissa (legal).

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachments: [MSA_v3_redline.docx (docx, ~28KB), OrderForm_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf, ~42KB)]

Subject: Re: End-of-commitment opt-out procedures & termination ops pocket guide

Naomi —

Appreciate the concise package. A couple quick points from our side:

- Procurement prefers a 60-day written notice for any non-renewal or opt-out.
- For termination for convenience, Lumen typically accepts a 30-day support window plus a pro-rata credit for unused committed months; any transition support beyond 30 days is handled under a short SOW.
- Please route DocuSign to procurement@lumenhealth.com and cc legal@acmecloud.com (our marketplace legal group is reviewing any platform T&Cs).

If you can update the redline to show a 60-day notice option and an explicit 30-day transitional support obligation, that would speed review on our end. Happy to do a quick call if you need to walk tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Cloud Integrations
Lumen Health

Subject: Re: End-of-commitment opt-out procedures & termination ops pocket guide

Ben —

Thanks, that direction helps. I pulled a short summary and proposed markup to accelerate internal legal review:

Summary of proposed changes (high-level):
- Auto-renew: Keep single 12-month renewal term but add a 60-day opt-out notice before renewal effective date (language in §2.1).
- Notice mechanics: Written notice via email + DocuSign notice considered effective when received by procurement@lumenhealth.com.
- TFC: Allow termination for convenience with 30 calendar days of standard transitional support (no additional charge) and pro-rata refund for pre-paid months beyond the termination effective date.
- Support handback: Redwood will provide reasonable assistance (knowledge transfer, export of config) for up to 30 days; additional support available under separate SOW at standard rates.

I attached a focused redline that: 1) shows the 60-day notice; 2) adds the TFC clause with the 30-day transitional support bucket; and 3) preserves our standard warranty and data return obligations. The goal is to be explicit about timing and to avoid ambiguous "reasonable notice" language.

Link to collaborative doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/optout-pocketguide-4821
Attachments: MSA_v3_redline.docx (see tracked changes)

If Lumen agrees to the 60-day default + 30-day transition, we can route the redline for signature. Marissa — tagging you to confirm the final wording is acceptable from a legal risk perspective (we're intentionally limiting exposure by capping transition support and offering pro-rata credits).

—Karthik
Sr. Manager, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: End-of-commitment opt-out procedures & termination ops pocket guide

Ben / Naomi —

Thanks for the context. I'm comfortable with the approach Karthik outlined with a couple of edits to limit open-ended obligations:

- Make the 60-day notice a hard deadline that applies only to auto-renewed terms; non-renewal before initial term still follows the same 60-day notice for consistency.
- For TFC: Redwood will provide 30 calendar days of transition support at no charge; any additional days require a signed SOW. We will include a cap on support hours (e.g., 120 hours) during the free transition to avoid indefinite obligations.
- Refund mechanics: pro-rata refund to be calculated on an unused days basis (not months) from payment date; specify the payment method used for the refund path.
- DocuSign routing: we'll prepare an envelope with incremental initialing on §2.1 (notice) and §7.3 (termination) so procurement and legal can initial the two clauses they care about.

I'll incorporate these edits into the redline and start the DocuSign envelope. Next steps:

1) Naomi — finalize whether Lumen wants explicit cap (120 hours) or no cap.
2) Ben / Procurement — confirm the recipient for signature (procurement@lumenhealth.com) and the internal legal reviewer (legal@acmecloud.com).
3) Once confirmed, I'll send DocuSign (Deal DL-4821) and include the two attachments: MSA_v3_redline.docx and OrderForm_SOW_v2.pdf.

Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts — Redwood Inference
